title: From Car Park to Night Market
paras: In a small town in [[malaysia|Malaysia]], a night market began with a simple plan. In 1978, a cook named Farid wanted a place to sell his evening meals. A shop owner offered him a [[parking-lot|parking lot]] behind her shop after six. Farid helped [[arrange|arrange]] the first market with five other sellers. He sent invitations by [[post|post]] to friends in nearby towns, asking them to come.

At first, each seller brought a table and an oil lamp. Farid sold [[grilled|grilled]] fish with rice, while his neighbour sold sweet cakes. The smell brought people [[across|across]] the road from the houses opposite. Soon, the market became [[popular|popular]] with families. There were problems, too. After a table leg broke one evening, the sellers learned to [[fix|fix]] their own tables and keep spare wood nearby.

As the market grew, the shop owner put a large [[bin|bin]] beside the entrance for rubbish. Parents asked their children to [[behave|behave]] well and not run between the tables with hot pans on them. Years later, electric lights replaced the oil lamps, and more sellers joined. But one thing stayed the same: every evening, the cars left, the sellers set up their tables, and a quiet space became a place to eat together.
zh: 在马来西亚的一个小镇上，一处夜市始于一个简单的计划。1978年，一位名叫法里德的厨师想找个地方卖晚餐。一位店主让他在晚上六点后使用她店后的露天停车场。法里德和另外五位摊主一起筹备了第一次夜市。他通过邮寄的方式向附近城镇的朋友发出邀请，请他们来逛逛。
起初，每位摊主都带来一张桌子和一盏油灯。法里德卖烤鱼配米饭，旁边的摊主则卖甜糕。香味吸引了马路对面住宅里的人们，他们穿过马路来到夜市。很快，夜市就受到了许多家庭的欢迎。不过，也有一些问题。一天晚上，一条桌腿断了。此后，摊主们学着自己修桌子，并在附近备些木料。
随着夜市规模扩大，店主在入口旁放了一个大垃圾桶。家长们叮嘱孩子要守规矩，不要在摆着热锅的桌子之间奔跑。多年后，电灯取代了油灯，也有更多摊主加入。但有一件事没有改变：每天晚上，车子离开，摊主们摆好桌子，一处安静的空地就变成了大家一起吃饭的地方。

q.s: Farid paid the shop owner to use the parking lot.
q.why: 只说店主提供场地，未说明法里德是否付费。

q.s: Farid worked with other sellers to prepare the first market.
q.why: 首段说法里德与另外五位摊主共同筹备。

q.s: Electric lights were used at the market from the beginning.
q.why: 起初使用油灯，多年后才换成电灯。
